configuration_multiplier_boundary.setup: In fixed finite volume let H=P^2/(2chi)+V(Q), where V is the real semibounded coercive Q3 polynomial and H is self-adjoint. For f in C_b(R^d), let M_f be multiplication by f and alpha_t=Ad(exp(itH/hbar)).
configuration_multiplier_boundary.lower_bound: For every f in C_b(R^d), liminf_(t->0,t!=0)||alpha_t(M_f)-M_f||>=diam f(R^d).
configuration_multiplier_boundary.real_case: For every bounded continuous real f, the limit exists and equals osc(f)=sup f-inf f.
configuration_multiplier_boundary.proof: Fix x,y and a narrow Gaussian at x, boost it by p_t=chi(y-x)/t, and compare the full and free flows. The free packet reaches y while its spreading vanishes as t->0. Along |s|<=|t| the Galilean centers stay on a compact segment, so polynomial multiplication has a uniform Gaussian L2 bound and Duhamel costs O(|t|). Then send the Gaussian width to zero and take the supremum over x,y. For real f the scalar-midpoint upper bound equals osc(f).
